Regarding bladder stones, which of the following statements are true?
D is false: most bladder stones are fragmented endoscopically, but large or hard stones may need percutaneous or open cystolithotomy.

Calcium oxalate (alone or mixed with calcium phosphate) forms most urinary stones (about 75–80%), and these are radio-opaque.

Of these options, a plain KUB film is the initial test (about 90% of stones are radio-opaque); non-contrast CT KUB is now the definitive investigation.
Cystine
Gout (hyperuricosuria and persistently acidic urine) predisposes to uric acid stones, which are radiolucent on plain film but seen on CT.
